story.opened: 13 October 1922, opened by the Mayor, in a building converted from a Victorian asylum wing
story.then: According to the British Listed Buildings entry (reproducing Historic England's listing), Bethnal Green did not adopt the Public Libraries Act until 1913. A temporary library followed in 1919. The borough then bought part of the former Bethnal House Asylum estate and had its architect, A.E. Darby, convert the male wing, built in 1896, into a permanent library with lending, reference and children's sections, a lecture hall and a newsroom. The conversion cost £36,000.
story.now: The venue's own website advertises a collaboration between the library and Let's Discuss Death on 28 and 29 October 2026.
worth_knowing: British Listed Buildings gives the library's listing date as 14 January 2005.
